- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged value as anchor.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; add a “reversion” buffer (e.g., 1–3% downward correction after sentiment flip).
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility bias.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often drifts toward mean; use recent 7-day average as baseline for correction.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
